title: Reading an ECG — Rate, Rhythm and the Signs That Mean Stop

hook.en: In cardiac and ICU rehabilitation you will see ECG strips and monitors every day. Learn a five-step routine, the common rhythms and the changes that mean you stop exercise and call for help.
hook.ur: Cardiac aur ICU rehabilitation mein aap rozana ECG strips aur monitors dekhenge. Paanch qadam ki routine, aam rhythms aur woh tabdeeliyan seekhein jin ka matlab hai exercise rok kar madad bulayein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll find the heart rate on a strip, decide if the rhythm is regular and sinus, recognise atrial fibrillation, ST elevation and wide-complex tachycardia, and state when to stop and escalate.
goal.ur: End tak aap strip par heart rate nikalenge, faisla karenge ke rhythm regular aur sinus hai ya nahi, atrial fibrillation, ST elevation aur wide-complex tachycardia pehchanenge, aur batayenge ke kab rukna aur escalate karna hai.

text.en: An **ECG** records the **electrical activity** of the heart. On standard paper, **one small square is 0.04 seconds and one large square (five small) is 0.2 seconds**. The trace has a **P wave** (the atria contract), a **QRS complex** (the ventricles contract) and a **T wave** (the ventricles reset). A **12-lead ECG** looks at the heart from 12 angles; a **monitor strip** (often one or three leads) is used to watch the rhythm. Diagnosing from an ECG is the doctor's job; your job is to **spot a change, act safely and report**.
text.ur: **ECG** dil ki **bijli ki sargarmi** record karta hai. Standard kaghaz par **ek chhota khana 0.04 second aur ek bara khana (paanch chhote) 0.2 second** hota hai. Trace mein **P wave** (atria sikurte hain), **QRS complex** (ventricles sikurte hain) aur **T wave** (ventricles dobara taiyar hote hain) hote hain. **12-lead ECG** dil ko 12 zaviyon se dekhta hai; **monitor strip** (aksar ek ya teen lead) rhythm dekhne ke liye hota hai. ECG se tashkhees doctor ka kaam hai; aap ka kaam **tabdeeli pakarna, mehfooz kaarwai karna aur report karna** hai.

text.en: Think of the ECG as **a drumbeat you can see**. A healthy drummer keeps a steady beat: a small bump (P), a sharp spike (QRS) and a gentle hill (T), again and again. Trouble shows as a drummer who speeds up wildly, plays out of time, or whose pattern changes shape. You do not need to be a musician to notice that the beat has changed.
text.ur: ECG ko **aisi dhol ki thaap jo aap dekh sakte hain** samjhein. Sehatmand dhol-baaz musalsal beat rakhta hai: chhota ubhaar (P), tez spike (QRS) aur narm pahari (T), baar baar. Masla us dhol-baaz ki tarah nazar aata hai jo be-qaboo tez ho jaye, be-taal bajaye ya jis ke pattern ki shakl badal jaye. Beat badalne ko pehchanne ke liye musician hona zaroori nahi.

title.en: A five-step routine for a rhythm strip
title.ur: Rhythm strip ki paanch qadam ki routine

steps.title: Rate
steps.detail: Count the large squares between two R waves and divide 300 by that number, or count the QRS complexes in a 6-second strip and multiply by 10. A normal resting rate is about 60 to 100 beats a minute. || Rate

steps.title: Rhythm
steps.detail: Is the spacing between R waves even? Regular spacing suggests a regular rhythm; an "irregularly irregular" pattern with no clear pattern suggests atrial fibrillation. || Rhythm

steps.title: P waves
steps.detail: Is there a P wave before every QRS, of the same shape? If yes it is probably sinus rhythm; no P waves with an irregular rhythm suggests atrial fibrillation. || P waves

steps.title: QRS width and ST segment
steps.detail: Is the QRS narrow (under 3 small squares)? A wide, fast rhythm is dangerous. Is the ST segment flat, or raised or depressed compared with the baseline? New ST change can mean the heart muscle is short of oxygen. || QRS ki chaurai aur ST segment

question.en: A strip shows no P waves and a completely irregular rhythm at about 120 beats a minute. What is the most likely pattern?
question.ur: Strip par P waves nahi aur rhythm bilkul irregular, takreeban 120 dharkan fi minute. Sab se mumkin pattern kya hai?

feedback.en: Sinus rhythm has a P wave before each QRS and is regular.
feedback.ur: Sinus rhythm mein har QRS se pehle P wave hoti hai aur regular hoti hai.

feedback.en: That shows a slow regular rate.
feedback.ur: Isme dheemi regular rate hoti hai.

text.en: Atrial fibrillation with a fast ventricular rate
text.ur: Atrial fibrillation tez ventricular rate ke saath

feedback.en: Yes — an irregularly irregular rhythm without P waves is the classic pattern.
feedback.ur: Haan — P waves ke baghair irregularly irregular rhythm khaas pattern hai.

rows.en: Exercise as planned if no other signs
rows.ur: Dusri nishaniyan na hon to plan ke mutabiq exercise

rows.en: Know if it is known and controlled; new AF with symptoms needs medical review
rows.ur: Maloom aur qaboo mein hai ya nahi dekhein; alamaat ke saath naya AF medical review maangta hai

text.en: **Rate, rhythm, P, QRS, ST.** Work through the same five steps every time, and always ask how the patient is. A frightening trace in a patient who feels well and a normal trace in a patient with chest pain both need a doctor's input.
text.ur: **Rate, rhythm, P, QRS, ST.** Har baar wohi paanch qadam, aur hamesha mareez se poochhein woh kaisa hai. Mareez theek ho aur trace daraune ho, ya mareez ko seene ka dard ho aur trace normal ho, dono ko doctor ki raaye chahiye.

text.en: **Trusting the machine alone, or the number alone.** Monitors give false alarms when a lead falls off or the patient moves. Check the patient first (colour, pulse, breathing, symptoms), then the lead, then the trace. And a normal rate does not mean a normal rhythm.
text.ur: **Sirf machine ya sirf number par bharosa.** Lead gir jaye ya mareez hile to monitors ghalat alarm dete hain. Pehle mareez dekhein (rang, nabz, saans, alamaat), phir lead, phir trace. Aur normal rate ka matlab normal rhythm nahi.

question.en: During treadmill walking, a patient develops chest pain and the monitor shows new ST depression. What should you do?
question.ur: Treadmill par chalte hue mareez ko seene ka dard hota hai aur monitor par nayi ST depression nazar aati hai. Aap kya karein?

text.en: Stop the exercise, sit the patient down, check vital signs and call the medical team
text.ur: Exercise rokein, mareez ko bithayein, vital signs check karein aur medical team ko bulayein

feedback.en: Yes — new ST change with symptoms is a stop criterion.
feedback.ur: Haan — alamaat ke saath nayi ST tabdeeli rukne ka mayaar hai.

text.en: Increase the speed to see if it settles
text.ur: Rate barhayein ke dekhein theek hota hai

feedback.ur: Isse dil ko nuqsan ho sakta hai.

text.en: Ignore it if the rate is normal
text.ur: Rate normal ho to nazar andaz karein

feedback.en: Symptoms and ST change matter more than the rate.
feedback.ur: Alamaat aur ST tabdeeli rate se zyada ahem hain.

question.en: Which rhythm needs an emergency response straight away?
question.ur: Kaun si rhythm ko foran emergency jawab chahiye?

text.en: A sinus rate of 70 at rest
A fast wide-complex rhythm with a patient who is faint or unresponsive
text.ur: Tez, chauda QRS rhythm jab mareez behoshi jaisa ya be-jawab ho

feedback.en: Yes — this can be ventricular tachycardia or fibrillation and needs emergency care.
feedback.ur: Haan — yeh ventricular tachycardia ya fibrillation ho sakti hai aur emergency care maangti hai.

text.en: An occasional extra beat in a well patient
text.ur: Sehatmand mareez mein kabhi kabhi ek extra dharkan

feedback.en: That is common and usually harmless, but report frequent ones.
feedback.ur: Yeh aam aur aam taur par begarar hai, magar baar baar ho to report karein.

text.en: **Check, calm, call.** Check the patient and the trace, calm the patient (sit them down, reassure) and call for help early using your unit's rules. Record the rhythm, the patient's symptoms, the time and what you did. In an emergency, follow your resuscitation training.
text.ur: **Dekhein, sukoon dein, bulayein.** Mareez aur trace check karein, mareez ko sukoon dein (bithayein, tasalli dein) aur apni unit ke qawaid ke mutabiq jaldi madad bulayein. Rhythm, mareez ki alamaat, waqt aur jo kiya likhein. Emergency mein apni resuscitation ki training par chalein.

question.en: Why is a patient's symptom more important than a single odd-looking beat?
question.ur: Mareez ki alamat ek ajeeb dikhne wali dharkan se zyada ahem kyun hai?

answer.en: Occasional extra beats are common and often harmless, and a trace can be disturbed by movement. A patient with chest pain, faintness, breathlessness or a falling blood pressure, with or without a changed trace, may be in danger. The patient's condition sets the urgency.
answer.ur: Kabhi kabhi extra dharkanein aam aur aksar begarar hoti hain, aur harkat se trace kharab ho sakta hai. Seene ka dard, behoshi jaisi kaifiyat, saans ki tangi ya girta blood pressure wale mareez, trace badla ho ya na, khatre mein ho sakte hain. Mareez ki halat urgency tay karti hai.

beats.patient: A 64-year-old man is walking in cardiac rehabilitation 3 weeks after a heart attack. His rate rises from 80 to 120, the strip becomes irregular with no P waves and he feels light-headed. His blood pressure falls from 130 over 80 to 98 over 60.
beats.assessment: A new irregular rhythm with symptoms and a falling blood pressure needs a stop and urgent medical review.
beats.treatment: Stop, sit him down, check his observations, call the medical team and record the rhythm, symptoms and time.
beats.reassess: He is assessed, found to be in new atrial fibrillation, and his medicines are adjusted before exercise resumes.

text.en: **Stop exercise and call for help** for chest pain, severe breathlessness, faintness, a fall in blood pressure, new ST elevation or depression, a new fast or irregular rhythm with symptoms, or a wide-complex tachycardia. Call the emergency team straight away if the patient collapses or is unresponsive, and begin basic life support. Never leave a monitored patient with an unexplained rhythm change.
text.ur: **Exercise rokein aur madad bulayein** seene ka dard, shadeed saans ki tangi, behoshi jaisi kaifiyat, blood pressure ka girna, nayi ST elevation ya depression, alamaat ke saath nayi tez ya irregular rhythm, ya wide-complex tachycardia par. Mareez gir jaye ya be-jawab ho to foran emergency team bulayein aur basic life support shuru karein. Monitored mareez ko bina wajah rhythm tabdeeli ke akela na chhorein.

summary.en: An ECG shows the heart's electrical activity: P wave, QRS and T wave; use five steps: rate, rhythm, P waves, QRS width and ST segment.
summary.ur: ECG dil ki bijli ki sargarmi dikhata hai: P wave, QRS aur T wave; paanch qadam: rate, rhythm, P waves, QRS ki chaurai aur ST segment.

summary.en: Recognise sinus rhythm, atrial fibrillation (irregularly irregular, no P waves), ST changes and wide-complex tachycardia, and always check the patient first.
summary.ur: Sinus rhythm, atrial fibrillation (irregularly irregular, P waves nahi), ST tabdeeliyan aur wide-complex tachycardia pehchanein, aur hamesha pehle mareez check karein.

summary.en: Stop and call for help for symptoms with a new rhythm or ST change; a diagnosis is the doctor's job, not yours.
summary.ur: Nayi rhythm ya ST tabdeeli ke saath alamaat par rukein aur madad bulayein; tashkhees doctor ka kaam hai, aap ka nahi.
